review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–132). It has three theorems. None is a candidate simp lemma: they are iff or Subsingleton statements about universally quantified instance-heavy hypotheses, and they have no useful simp-normal form. The file declares no simp lemmas and no attributes, and it adds no competing rewrite rules. Its proofs call `simp` and `simpa` only on local goals. These use the existing Mathlib simp lemmas `nsmulAddMonoidHom_apply`, `AddSubgroup.coe_nsmul` and `AddSubgroup.coe_zero`. I looked for a missing canonical simp lemma, for example for `IsPPrimaryTorsion` and `nsmulAddMonoidHom`. I found only uses of `isPPrimaryTorsion_iff` in other files, and they apply it with `.1` or `.2`, so I could not show that a simp attribute would help any caller. I did not read the definition of `IsPPrimaryTorsion` or the SingleDegree file. I cannot run Lean, so I claim no observed simp behavior.
